Shared UI, states and design direction

Page-level specifications inherit this contract. Apply only the states relevant to the task; use an explicit N/A rationale instead of decorative empty/error screens. All new interaction details are proposed defaults for the first HTML.

Visual direction

Preserve Whiteboard teal, neutral surfaces, system typography, restrained hierarchy and realistic academic content. The original source tokens are in resources/design-system/. Historical comments saying “proposal/not accepted” are preserved provenance; the owner later accepted the original visual direction. New page layouts still need review.

Light palette: page #f3f4f5, surface #ffffff, ink #16191b, secondary ink #575e63, identity teal #007176, focus blue #0a66d8. Dark palette: page #0f1112, surface #1b1e20, ink #eef1f2, teal #5cc8c8. Do not use the dark fill color as label text on a light background without checking the relevant pair.

Use system sans-serif with a compact but readable hierarchy: proposed web body 16px, secondary 14px, page title 28-32px, section title 18-20px, 1.45-1.6 body line-height. Older references use a 15px web body; the proposed 16px is an intentional new starting default. Prefer 4px spacing increments. Keep primary forms around 640-760px, reading text around 65-80 characters per line, and allow staff work tables to use the available desktop width.

Coursework lists should look like readable work lists; grades should be a structured table; calendars should have a visible agenda alternative; grading should prioritize evidence and score entry. Avoid styling every page as a grid of identical dashboard cards. Use actual course names, dates and specimen work, not marketing text or arbitrary metrics. No remote fonts, decorative stock images or icon library dependencies are needed. The initial mark can be typographic Whiteboard; a new brand logo is not required.

The frontend developer may improve spacing, typography and visual treatment while preserving semantics, contrast, task hierarchy and workflow rules. Keep tokens separate from content and behavior. Do not redraw the existing iPhone frames for this web-only task.

Layout and responsive behavior

  • Desktop: persistent sidebar, compact top bar, task-specific canvas. 1280-1440px is a useful design starting width, not a fixed requirement. Grading may use roster/evidence/score panes when space allows.
  • Intermediate width: collapse secondary rails into sections or drawers with the same headings and context. Do not silently remove learner identity, score maxima, due dates or save status.
  • Narrow web: around 320-768 CSS pixels, use a navigation disclosure and stacked content. Keep primary actions reachable and labeled. This is responsive web, not a native tab-bar promise.
  • Gradebook/data matrices may scroll within a labeled region while the surrounding page reflows. Preserve column headers/row identity. Provide a focused single-learner view on narrow screens. Staff bulk editing remains best on desktop, with an explicit usable narrow alternative for review/protective actions.
  • Keyboard, sticky actions and zoom must not cover the focused field or error. Avoid horizontal page scrolling for ordinary text/forms. Render long course titles, filenames, equations, translated-length labels and large grades without clipping.
  • Light/dark preference follows system or explicit setting. Respect reduced motion. Motion answers the user's action; no continuous decorative motion is needed.

Reusable components

ComponentRequired anatomy and behavior
Course context headerCode/title, term/section, current role, publication/read-only indicator, breadcrumb and relevant next action.
Assessment rowTitle, kind, personal due date/time zone, submission/grade status, relevant score only when authorized, one clear primary link.
Status badgeIcon plus words; color is secondary. Held feedback is neutral. Never make “Queued” visually equivalent to “Received.”
FieldPersistent label, required/optional meaning, helper text, current value and associated inline error. Do not use placeholder as label.
Validation summaryOne top summary with links to invalid fields; preserve values. Explain the fix. Errors block the consequential action; warnings require a deliberate review when appropriate.
TableCaption, headers and row identity; proper semantic table by default. Sort buttons announce current direction. Do not add role=grid unless implementing its full keyboard model.
Dialog/drawerNamed title, concise effect, clear confirm/cancel, focus enters and returns logically. Modal content makes background inert; close affordance and Escape behavior are explicit.
Upload queueFilename/type/size, progress per file, processing/error status, retry/remove, alternative input and accessible equivalent. Drag/drop is optional enhancement.
Evidence viewerPage/file list, selected page/question, zoom/rotation and full text alternative; drawing annotation is optional for first HTML, typed comments are required.
Date/time controlExplicit zone and local interpretation, start/end validation, all-day option, recurrence exceptions and personal/course authority. Do not rely only on a dense visual calendar picker.
Draft/save indicatorLast sample save time, dirty/saving/saved locally/failed/conflict states. Saves never imply final submission or publication.
Release previewExact learner/attempt/score/comment/rubric payload, exclusions and version fingerprint. Relevant changes invalidate it.
Activity itemHuman-readable event, source/course, time, unread state, safe destination. Never expose a grade in notification preview.
Tool access cardVerified product/course purpose, eligibility, institutional account requirement, access instructions, owner/support, expiry and external-site label.
Scenario toolbarSeparate prototype chrome for role, record state, failure injection and reset. Never mix these controls into the product's permission model.

State vocabulary and recovery

StateRequired presentation and next action
LoadingStable content skeleton/status for the affected region; do not show fabricated grades or “0” while data is unknown.
First-use emptyExplain what is absent and who can create it. A student cannot receive an instructor-only Create button.
Filtered emptyName active filters; offer Clear filters. Distinguish from having no course data.
InvalidShow exact field error and summary, keep entered values, focus the right field and block only the invalid action.
Saving / local saveShow where the data currently exists. A local draft is not a server acknowledgment.
Save failedRetain draft, describe what was not saved, retry safely or copy permitted text. Never offer false success.
Conflict/staleIdentify the newer version and affected record. Offer compare/reload/keep local draft where safe. Never silently overwrite marks or receipts.
OfflineLabel cached/last-known information. Block final send/release where acknowledgment is required; preserve eligible draft work and explain resume.
Permission unavailableState course/role boundary without leaking other people's private data. Provide safe return/help; mutation remains blocked on direct entry.
Session expiring/expiredWarn without losing work; institutional sign-in return restores an allowed destination and verifies latest state before retry.
Not yet availableName date/prerequisite if the learner is allowed to know it; do not expose hidden answers/material.
ArchivedShow term and read-only policy. Keep allowed historical feedback and receipts; do not invent permanent retention.
SuccessName the actual sample change and next destination. Submissions need receipt; releases need recipient/version history; scheduling needs publication state.
Partial bulk successShow item-level successes/failures; retry failed items only. No “All done” toast while rows remain unresolved.
Denied device permissionOffer file/manual/keyboard alternative. Do not repeatedly request permission or imply user refusal is a course failure.
Destructive actionName scope/count/record and whether reversible. Preserve history where required; Cancel returns without change.

Copy examples: “Upload interrupted. Your 3 selected pages are still in this draft. Retry upload.” “Preview changed. Review the new scores before releasing.” “You can grade assigned questions until Oct 18, 11:59 pm ET. Only the instructor can restore access.” Avoid generic “Something went wrong” without a recovery.

Dates, counters and notification behavior

Store timestamps with an unambiguous zone/offset in fixtures. Display institution zone and personal adjustments clearly; use local dates for all-day items. Due/close and quiz timer settings are separate. Grading deadlines must not change student due dates. A delayed external class schedule should show its last-known timestamp; coursework owned by Whiteboard should not inherit that source's delay label.

Reminders reference an event/version, so moving or cancelling a class invalidates pending reminders. Notification preference changes affect future delivery, not the underlying course record. In HTML, simulate permission granted/denied and delivery pending/failed; no real email/push is required. A read activity item remains traceable to its source. Personal planning data is private even if the user has a staff role in the course.

Accessibility contract

Target WCAG 2.2 AA as a design/implementation goal. This is not a conformance claim or a statement of the institution's legal obligations. Use semantic landmarks/headings, visible labels, keyboard operation, focus visibility, names for icon controls and programmatic status/error associations. Aim for 44px touch controls as a design choice; WCAG 2.2's minimum target rule has different sizing/spacing exceptions. [M01](../research/core-evidence.md), [M09](../research/core-evidence.md).

Use named dialogs with deliberate focus management, a full keyboard alternative to dragging/reordering, and concise error notifications. A plain semantic grade table is preferable to an incomplete spreadsheet keyboard model. [M02-M04](../research/core-evidence.md).

Check 200% text enlargement and reflow at 320 CSS pixels, with contained two-dimensional tables where genuinely needed. Test screen-reader task completion rather than inferring it from ARIA attributes. [M05](../research/core-evidence.md).

Provide text equivalents for handwritten/PDF specimens, captions/transcripts for teaching media and understandable typed math. Keep timers perceivable without announcing every second; allowance and timed-assessment exception behavior needs institutional review. Never disable copy/paste in authentication or force memory puzzles in the prototype. [M10](../research/core-evidence.md).

Detailed component behavior above is the team's proposed contract informed by the linked guidance. Run actual keyboard, screen-reader, zoom, contrast, forced-color and viewport review before claiming acceptance.
